structure:
[part 1] Kentucky Academic Standards for Social Studies (Dec 2022). Front matter (TOC, introduction, legal basis, vision, organization, inquiry-practice and discipline-strand definitions, coding explanation) precedes grade sections. K-5 and 6-8 band overviews each have a Grade-level Introductions page. Each grade K-8 has three parts: (1) '<Grade>: <Theme>' title + 'Specific Overview' (introduction, key vocabulary, looking back/ahead, 'What this would look like in practice' table with Standard / Sample Evidence of Learning columns, Opportunities for Cross-Disciplinary Connections); (2) '<Grade>: <Theme> Standards' with an Introduction paragraph and a 'Concepts and Practices | Standards' table whose first column names the practice/concept (I: Questioning, I: Investigating, I: Using Evidence, I: Communicating Conclusions; C: / E: / G: / H: strand concepts such as Civic and Political Institutions (CP), Microeconomics (MI), Migration and Movement (MM), Change and Continuity (CH), Kentucky strands KGO/KE/KGE/KH) and whose standards column holds codes of the form <grade>.<strand>.<concept>.<n> (e.g. K.C.CP.1, 4.G.MM.1, 8.H.CO.4; inquiry codes <grade>.I.Q/UE/CC.<n>); (3) '<Grade>: Disciplinary Clarifications and Instructional Support' with Civics/Economics/Geography/History strand tables (Concepts and Practices | Standard | Disciplinary Clarifications) that repeat each standard beside its clarification. Inquiry standards are repeated per grade (no separate K-12 shared block in this range). High school sections and Appendix A progressions fall after this range (from u2355). Labeling choices: grade title headings and the Concepts-and-Practices standards tables = standards; introductions, Specific Overview material, sample-evidence tables and clarification tables (including the standard text copied into them) = examples; explanatory sentence under each clarifications heading = backup.
[part 2] Kentucky Academic Standards for Social Studies (2019, rev. 2022). Grades K-8 each have a 'Grade N: <Theme> Standards' section (Inquiry Practices + discipline strands Civics/Economics/Geography/History) in a 2-column table 'Concepts and Practices | Standards', then a separate 'Grade N: Disciplinary Clarifications and Instructional Support' section (3-column table adding 'Disciplinary Clarifications'; labeled examples, including the standard text repeated in column 2). Standard codes: <grade>.<discipline>.<concept>.<n> (e.g. 8.C.CP.1, 8.H.KH.2); inquiry practices <grade>.I.Q/UE/CC.n. High school has an overview then five course sections (Civics, Economics, Geography, United States History, World History) each with an introduction, a standards table (codes HS.C/E/G/UH/WH.<concept>.<n>; inquiry HS.X.I.Q/UE/CC; US/World History start with a time-period/theme table) and a Disciplinary Clarifications section (examples); all HS content is grades 9-12 with course = discipline name. In table extraction the strand/concept name (C1) sits in separate units near the row, often split over several rows. Appendix A is K-12 progressions (inquiry Q/UE/CC, then Civics, Economics, Geography, History) first by grade level then by concept, as tables with Grade Level | Concepts and Practices | Standards columns where grade labels and strand labels are scattered across rows near the standards; these repeat the standards and are labeled examples with the grade of each row (HS rows 9-12 with the course). Appendices B and C are committee lists (backup).
